## referenceResultType() function

The value type of what a reference resolves to, from the output of the operation it resolves as: for `'one'`<!-- -->, that operation's (a `get`<!-- -->'s) output; for `'many'`<!-- -->, an array of the items of that operation's (a `list`<!-- -->'s) page.

**Signature:**

```typescript
declare function referenceResultType(
  cardinality: ReferenceCardinality,
  output: ValueType<unknown>
): ValueType<unknown>
```

**Returns:**

[ValueType](./contracts.valuetype.md)<!-- -->&lt;unknown&gt;

The value type of the resolution's result.

## Exceptions

`TypeError` when `cardinality` is `'many'` and `output` is neither a page (`t.page(…)`<!-- -->) nor `passthrough`<!-- -->: the contract's list operation does not have the shape every list has, so it must be regenerated.

## Remarks

This is the one statement of what a resolution returns. A collection reference is not paged: it resolves to every member of its selection, an array possibly empty, never one page of it, even though the `list` operation it resolves as returns pages when called directly. The runtime validates a resolution's result against this type and hands its plan to the executor, and a client decodes the result with it.

An output with a `passthrough` plan has no wire encoding and is returned unchanged for either cardinality.
